clue.text: The last appalling secret procedure

indicators.note: appalling describes something dreadful or messed up, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone describes a final, shocking clandestine operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges THE LAST; the opening words look like the subject of the sentence but are only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is the quality of acting covertly, so it fits a hidden or furtive way of doing things.

clue.text: Beautiful female, look!

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'

explanation.surface: Someone admires a lovely woman and urges a companion to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' reads as an exclamation, but it is the noun sense, someone's appearance or manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old-fashioned word for lovely or comely, as in 'fair maiden'.

clue.text: Talk about the French holiday accommodation

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the word for talk surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to chat is to talk informally
LE is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: People discuss French holiday lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', as if people were talking about the French, but it means going round. 'the French' is a stock crossword way to ask for the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, typically rented by skiers or other holidaymakers.

clue.text: Go kitted out with anorak or jumper

indicators.note: kitted out suggests something dressed up or rearranged, so the letters of the neighbouring words are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is told to set off wearing a waterproof jacket or a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitted out' rearranges GO and ANORAK together. 'jumper' looks like a British pullover sweater, which suits the clothing picture, but it means an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The kangaroo moves by hopping on its powerful hind legs, so it is a famous leaper.

clue.text: Name actors mingling in Californian location

indicators.note: mingling means mixing together, so the letters of these two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Performers mixing at a party in a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mingling' rearranges NAME ACTORS; actors mixing in California suggests Hollywood, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California.

clue.text: Number one story coming up to bring delight

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A top-selling story arrives to bring joy to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole of NO + I + TALE, giving NOITALE read upwards. 'Number one' looks like a phrase meaning 'best', but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and joy.

clue.text: A dry sort of person longing to become a diplomat

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, describing someone who drinks no alcohol, so is dry
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A dull, yearning individual aspires to a career in diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like 'dull' or 'witty', but here it means teetotal, abbreviated TT.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is an embassy staff member, a junior member of a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Forbid colleague in a boring way

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone tediously bans a co-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, so the adverb describes doing something dully.

clue.text: Possibly a new thicker set of culinary items

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fresh, chunkier collection of cooking equipment is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges A NEW THICKER, all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchenware is the collective term for pots, pans and utensils used in cooking.

clue.text: Irishman on wheels doing guard duty

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock name for an Irishman
something moving on wheels is rolling

explanation.surface: An Irishman on a bicycle or in a car is keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: PAT is a traditional nickname for an Irishman in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrolling means walking or driving round an area to guard it.

clue.text: Scoundrels knocking celebrity over

indicators.note: over, with knocking, suggests something toppled and turned round, so the word for celebrity is read backwards

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Villains topple a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking ... over' turns STAR round; 'knocking' surrounds the word for celebrity along with 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats is slang for treacherous or despicable people.

clue.text: Vigorous soccer team in Charlton

explanation.surface: A lively football club in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlton Athletic is a London football club; the second definition names the word that follows Charlton in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic means strong and energetic, and it is also the second part of Charlton Athletic, a London football club.

clue.text: Rank place in France given to leaseholder

parts.note: lieu is the French word for place
a tenant holds property under a lease

explanation.surface: A French property is handed over to someone renting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, but it is a noun: a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a military officer's grade, below captain.

clue.text: One should be able to get through a barrel

definitions.text: One should be able to get through a barrel

parts.words: One should be able to get through a barrel
parts.note: the surface suggests someone drinking a whole barrel of beer, but it is a rod used to push the charge down the barrel of a gun

explanation.walkthrough: 'get through a barrel' sounds like heavy drinking; the barrel is a gun's.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is a rod used to push shot and powder down the bore of a muzzle-loading firearm.

clue.text: Understand and receive available mark

explanation.surface: A player both grasps the rules and collects the score on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: get (receive) the point (the mark available).
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp what someone means is to see their meaning; literally, it is also to be awarded a scoring unit.

clue.text: Like loud music that's come on the scene

explanation.surface: Music at full volume, which has just appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is volume increased; the other is the idiom for arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume that has been raised is louder, and to appear or arrive somewhere is also expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Holy Indian mother collects something from the milliner

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so the word for mother holds the other piece

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
a milliner makes and sells hats

explanation.surface: An Indian mother picks up a purchase from a hat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' suggests picking up a parcel from the shop; here it means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning 'great soul', is a title of respect for a revered Indian sage, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Listen to a number and take courage

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a count and feels braver.
explanation.walkthrough: Any number could be meant; the crossing letters settle on TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten can mean to take heart, becoming encouraged and bolder.

clue.text: Minister is quiet when meeting Nancy, MP

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical marking for quiet
Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat as a British MP

explanation.surface: A clergyman stays silent on meeting a famous woman politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a government post beside the MP, but it means a clergyman. Nancy Astor sat in Parliament from 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a church minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Jazz pianist without work — one who really pounds the keys?

definitions.text: one who really pounds the keys?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the pianist's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Fats Waller was an American jazz pianist
OP, for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist out of work hammers the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', as if the pianist were unemployed, but in its old sense it means outside. Fats Waller was a 1930s American stride pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: A walloper is someone who hits hard, so the question mark marks a pianist who strikes the keys forcefully.

clue.text: What we have during quieter periods reading

definitions.text: What we have during quieter periods

explanation.surface: Something done in calmer moments, such as reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: when there is less on, things are quieter. The second is a Bible passage read in church.
explanation.definitionFit: In church, a passage of scripture read aloud is called this; and a quieter time is when there is less happening.

clue.text: This may be the time for waking up girl

definitions.text: This may be the time for waking up

explanation.surface: A woman's name and the hour for rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when many people wake, and it is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Special ruler's coat seen in exhibition centre

indicators.note: special suggests something made unusual, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch's distinctive robe is put on display at an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges RULERS COAT. EARLS COURT is a former exhibition hall in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court was a major London exhibition venue, home to shows like the Ideal Home Show.

clue.text: Frank is absorbed by telescope nightly

indicators.note: is absorbed by means the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: An astronomer named Frank is engrossed by his telescope every night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is an adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid and plain-spoken, a frank person is honest and forthright.

clue.text: Almost don't use commonsense, being sinister

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to omit something is to leave it out, not use it
nous is practical intelligence or good sense

explanation.surface: A warning that failing to use good sense is threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from OMIT, giving OMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening or foreboding, suggesting something bad will happen.

clue.text: Old-fashioned man communist protected

parts.note: cove is dated British slang for a man or chap
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: An old-style gentleman who is a communist is sheltered.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is old British slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered means shielded or sheltered from harm.
